vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: web-collection
Version: 1.2.2

The skill bundle provides a complex framework for web data collection with high-risk capabilities, including remote command execution via SSH and communication with an external cloud API. The 'run.sh' script supports a remote mode that executes shell commands on a user-provided host via SSH, and 'cloud_dispatch_loop.sh' transmits user API tokens to 'https://i-sync.cn'. While these features appear aligned with the stated purpose of a distributed scraping 'connector' system, the combination of credential handling, remote execution, and interaction with the user's primary browser profile (as instructed in SKILL.md) creates a significant security risk and attack surface.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (browser-extension-based web collection) mostly matches its scripts, but there are multiple coherence and privacy concerns — notably use of the user's normal Chrome profile, an undocumented cloud backend (i-sync.cn) as a default, and storage/usage of API tokens that are not declared in the registry metadata.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the included scripts: the code implements a local bridge flow and a cloud dispatch flow for browser-extension collection. However the skill expects sensitive inputs (cloud API token / connector admin token) and to operate inside the user's "normal Chrome environment" — both are high-privacy operations and are not represented in the registry metadata (no required env/primary credential listed). The hard-coded default cloud base URL (https://i-sync.cn) is external and not documented in the skill metadata or homepage.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to use the user's normal Chrome environment (not an isolated profile), to request and store a cloud API token (defaultCloudToken) and to interact with a local connector (localhost:19820) and a cloud dispatch API. The docs and scripts reference reading local connector admin token files (e.g. ~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt) and require writing/reading preferences under ~/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json. These instructions go beyond a simple integration and involve reading/writing local state and driving a browser extension that can access user data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external installer or remote download (instruction-only with bundled scripts). That reduces supply-chain risk. The scripts are executed locally and require curl/node; nothing is fetched from unknown URLs during install. However the skill includes runnable scripts with network behavior and remote/SSH options, so execution will perform network ops when invoked.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars or primary credential, but the skill expects/uses several secrets/values at runtime: defaultCloudToken (user API key) and optionally a bridge admin token read from a local file. The cloud token is stored in the preferences JSON under the user's .openclaw state directory. This mismatch between declared requirements and actual expected credentials is a notable coherence issue and a potential secret-exfiltration risk if the cloud endpoint or dispatch flow is untrusted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes preferences and tokens to $OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json (or fallback $HOME/.openclaw/...). Storing tokens locally is functionally reasonable for repeated use, but increases persistence of sensitive data. The skill does not set always:true and does not modify other skills' configurations, but it can be instructed to start a local bridge command or run via SSH (optional remote execution), which increases the blast radius when combined with the other concerns.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: 1) Treat it as high-privacy: it will try to drive a browser extension in your normal Chrome profile (which can access cookies, logins, and other private data). Prefer a separate browser profile or avoid the feature if you cannot segregate data. 2) The default cloud backend is https://i-sync.cn — do not provide API tokens or device IDs unless you trust that domain/organization. 3) The skill stores API tokens under ~/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json; if you supply tokens, they will persist on disk (masked when shown but stored in cleartext JSON). Consider using ephemeral tokens and remove them after use. 4) The scripts can invoke a local bridge (localhost:19820) and optionally start a bridge process with a user-supplied command or run remotely via SSH — only allow these if you trust the code being run. 5) If you need this functionality, prefer local mode (no cloud dispatch) and audit the extension/connector code itself. Do not paste secrets into chat messages; instead populate credentials in a controlled environment (environment variables or files) and inspect the preference file before and after use. If you are unsure, decline or ask the skill author for an auditable security/privacy whitepaper and the exact purpose of the i-sync.cn backend.
llm.findings:
[CLOUD_BASE_URL_HARDCODED] expected: A cloud dispatch flow needs a base URL; the default is hard-coded to https://i-sync.cn in SKILL.md and scripts. That's expected for cloud mode, but the domain is external and not documented elsewhere (no homepage); verify you trust that backend before providing tokens.
[LOCAL_BRIDGE_ADMIN_TOKEN_READ] expected: SKILL.md and example commands reference reading an admin token file (~/.meixi-connector/bridge-admin-token.txt) for local requests. That is expected for a local connector administration flow but is sensitive (local token grants connector admin access).
[USES_NORMAL_CHROME_PROFILE] expected: The skill explicitly instructs the agent to use the user's normal Chrome environment (not an isolated profile). This is required to let a browser extension access user's real browsing data, but it is a privacy risk that should be highlighted to users.
[STORES_CLOUD_TOKEN_IN_PREFERENCES] unexpected: The export_preference.sh script reads/writes defaultCloudToken to ~/.openclaw/skill-state/web-collection/preferences.json. Storing tokens locally is functionally plausible, but the skill registry metadata did not declare required credentials or primaryEnv, creating a transparency gap.
